Crie um site One Page totalmente funcional e profissional para a produtora Guizera Films.
O site deve ter estética moderna, ousada e cinematográfica, combinando minimalismo com impacto visual, animações suaves e contraste de luz e sombra.

🎨 Identidade visual

Use exatamente esta paleta de cores:

Roxo primário: #990adc

Roxo escuro: #600db1

Azul profundo: #171876

Branco: #ffffff

Vinho escuro / Preto púrpura: #140424

Utilize gradientes cinematográficos misturando #990adc → #600db1 → #171876.

Tipografia moderna

Defina fontes Google modernas e profissionais, como:

Headings: Montserrat, Poppins ou Sora

Texto: Inter, Lato ou Manrope

Alto contraste, peso forte nos títulos e leve no texto.

🏗️ Estrutura do site (One Page)
1. Hero (capa impactante)

Fundo com gradiente cinematográfico ou textura escura suave.

Título forte: “Guizera Films”.

Subtítulo: Produtora audiovisual especializada em vídeos políticos, institucionais, eventos e conteúdo digital.

Botão chamativo: Ver Portfólio (scroll para a seção de vídeos).

Animações suaves (fade in, parallax ou movimento horizontal leve).

2. Sobre

Texto breve apresentando a essência da produtora:

Quem é o fundador (Gui Azevedo)

Foco em estratégia + produção

Diferenciais: autenticidade, impacto emocional, qualidade, agilidade

Abordagem cinematográfica e profissional

3. Portfólio – Vídeos via Google Drive

Crie uma área onde o usuário pode colar um link público do Google Drive e o site automaticamente exiba o player do vídeo.

Exemplo de embed que o site deve aceitar:

https://drive.google.com/file/d/ID_DO_VIDEO/preview


Cada vídeo deve aparecer em cards com:

Miniatura automática do Drive

Player incorporado

Título opcional

Categoria (Institucional, Casamento, Evento, Político, YouTube etc.)

4. Portfólio – Vídeos via Instagram

Crie uma área onde é possível incorporar vídeos/Reels do Instagram apenas colando o link.

O site deve aceitar embeds usando o formato padrão de incorporação do Instagram.

Cada card deve exibir:

Vídeo/Reel incorporado

Legenda curta opcional

Nome do cliente ou projeto

5. Serviços

Liste os principais serviços da produtora:

Vídeos institucionais

Vídeos políticos

Vídeos de eventos

Publicidade e conteúdo comercial

Edição profissional

Conteúdos para YouTube e redes sociais

Use ícones modernos e elegantes.

6. Contato

Crie uma seção com:

Botão para WhatsApp

Formulário simples (Nome / E-mail / Mensagem)

Link para Instagram @guizerafilms

Rodapé leve e elegante

🎥 Funcionalidades obrigatórias

Players integrados para vídeos do Google Drive e do Instagram.

Site 100% responsivo.

Animações suaves e sem exagero.

Navegação por scroll e botões de âncora.

Paleta e fontes definidas acima.

Visual moderno + atmosfera cinematográfica (contraste, sombras, luzes, gradientes).

🔧 Tecnologia

Você pode construir com:

Framer

Webflow

WordPress com IA

Ou qualquer gerador de site baseado em IA

O código final deve ser limpo, responsivo, organizado e profissional.

📌 Objetivo final

Entregar um site impressionante, funcional e pronto para o cliente visualizar:

Vídeos do Drive sem bloqueio de direitos autorais

Vídeos do Instagram como portfólio

Visual cinematográfico moderno

Experiência de marca sólida e profissional

**Envisioning the Goal**

I'm now zeroing in on the core objective: a sleek, one-page web presence for Guizera Films. The focus is purely on showcasing their video production expertise in a professional and compelling way. This is the foundation upon which everything else will be built.


**Designing the Aesthetic**

I'm now deep-diving into the visual language. I've landed on a modern, cinematic style with a minimalist approach, embracing high-contrast elements and smooth animations. My color palette is set: a bold purple, deep blue, and a touch of white and dark wine. For typography, I'm considering Montserrat/Poppins/Sora for headings and Inter/Lato/Manrope for the body. The structure is taking shape, with sections for the hero, about, portfolio (Google Drive and Instagram embeds), services, and contact. Tech-wise, React with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS seems like the best fit. I'm focusing on dynamic video embedding from Google Drive and Instagram.


**Refining Video Display**

I'm now thinking about how to handle video display.  A CMS-like feature is out for this static React demo.  Instead, I'll use a state-based "Add Video" feature to demonstrate the ability to add and embed videos.  I'll preload some example data to showcase the functionality from the start.



**Optimizing Visuals & Tech**

I'm now focusing on the finer points of the design and tech. I've decided to go with a subtle gradient background using Tailwind, utilizing 'Sora' for headings and 'Manrope' for body text. I'll integrate `lucide-react` for clean icons and rely on standard CSS transitions for smooth animations. I'm also confirming the Google Drive and Instagram embedding strategy using iframes, with ID extraction for Google Drive videos.


**Clarifying Embedding Logic**

I'm working on the video embedding process. For Instagram, it's straightforward: just append `/embed` to the post URL within an iframe. For Google Drive, I'll use the iframe approach, but extracting the video ID might be needed. I'm focusing on dynamic video addition in the portfolio with state management, so users can add links as requested. I've sketched out the colors, fonts, and component structure, including a big gradient hero, services grid, and portfolio with both Drive and Instagram iframe sections, pre-filled with dummy data.


**Finalizing Video Input**

I'm now fully focused on the "Add Video" functionality. I've decided on a streamlined approach: a simple form with an input field and a button within the portfolio sections. This will update the state, leading to a new video card rendering. I've sketched out the `metadata.json` and basic HTML with the Tailwind CDN and custom config for colors via a script tag. Next I will set up the main React app structure, including the `types.ts` for interfaces and UI components. Finally, I will address the overall structure of the sections, separating components into different files.


**Defining Embedding Strategies**

I've nailed down the embedding logic for both platforms. For Google Drive, I'll extract the ID using a regex and craft the preview URL. Instagram's shortcode will also be regex-extracted and used for an iframe. I've opted for the iframe method for Instagram to ensure consistent rendering.

\n\n

**Finalizing the UI**

I'm now polishing the visual details. The header will feature a blur effect. The primary background will be a dark wine hue to make the purples stand out. Heading text will incorporate subtle gradients. I've re-reviewed everything against the project constraints, ensuring React 18+, TypeScript, and Tailwind are all utilized, and the one-page design with specific colors and functionality are adhered to.


**Assembling the Structure**

I'm now putting together the core files. I'm building out `metadata.json`, the `index.html` with custom Tailwind colors and the fonts (Sora and Manrope). Now I'm populating the React app's main file and its type definitions. I'm writing utility functions for URL parsing.  I'm focusing on crafting the components: a basic `Button`, `Section` to reduce code reuse, and then the actual content components like `Hero`, `About`, `Services`, and specialized `Portfolio` components for both Google Drive and Instagram videos. I'm also including `Contact` and `Footer` sections, alongside the `Header` component. Next, I'll integrate these components in `App.tsx`.

My current direction is to implement a client-side solution to toggle the visibility of the input fields, ensuring they remain hidden from the end-user. I'm exploring different JavaScript approaches to accomplish this.


**Developing an Admin Feature**

I'm now leaning towards a more robust "Edit Mode" triggered by a hidden element interaction or a URL query parameter. This approach ensures regular visitors don't see the input fields, while allowing the owner full control. Considering the static nature of the app, this offers a clean, client-side solution. I'll need to update the React component accordingly to check for this "edit mode" state and conditionally render the input fields.


**Considering CMS Alternatives**

I'm now contemplating alternative solutions. Removing the inputs outright isn't ideal. I'm weighing options for a simple CMS-like feature. Option B, an "Admin" toggle (hidden button or query parameter check), seems elegant and fulfills the requirement of clean, professional code. Option C, using a separate config file, is also under consideration. It would remove direct manipulation, yet requires no UI for regular users.


**Establishing Admin Access**

I've realized the "Admin Mode" is the optimal approach, as requested. The plan's coming together. I'll implement a straightforward `isAdmin` state, triggered by a URL parameter, probably `?admin=true`. This avoids a complex CMS, keeps the codebase clean, and addresses the "add" button visibility requirement. I'm passing this state as a prop to `PortfolioDrive.tsx` and `PortfolioInsta.tsx`. I'm now focusing on a crucial aspect. While I've implemented the `isAdmin` flag and `localStorage` persistence, I realize a fundamental limitation exists. Adding videos in admin mode saves them only for the admin's browser, not for all users. This stems from the static nature of the site and the absence of a backend database. I'm focusing on `App.tsx`, `PortfolioDrive.tsx`, and `PortfolioInsta.tsx` to handle the admin flag and video list enhancements. I'm cleaning up the placeholder logic to ensure it's robust.


**Completing the Integration**

I'm making progress wrapping up the `isAdmin` integration.  I've added the prop to `PortfolioDrive.tsx` and `PortfolioInsta.tsx` as planned, using conditional rendering based on the flag's value. I'm focusing on the final touches, and handling cases for any unexpected `null` or undefined values.  I've added `localStorage` to ensure added videos persist for admins.


**Finalizing Admin Interface**

I'm now fully immersed in the final touches. I've addressed the admin-mode banner, adding a discreet "Modo Edição Ativo" indicator to `App.tsx` when `isAdmin` is true.  I've also reviewed the dummy data in `PortfolioDrive` to make the site look like it's ready. The "adding" function only persists locally, but the client might want a simple interface.


**Developing the Admin Trigger**

My focus is now on the `App.tsx` and related components, where I'm aiming for a simple admin mode. I'm exploring adding a very subtle, almost invisible admin "link" to the URL via the footer. This avoids a complex CMS, yet allows for easy toggling of the admin view. I'll ensure that the URL check and parameter handling in `App.tsx` accurately control the visibility of the input fields in the portfolio components.

**Verifying Type Signatures**

I'm now diligently updating the type signatures to include the `isAdmin` prop. I'm modifying `PortfolioDrive.tsx` and `PortfolioInsta.tsx`, converting them from `React.FC` to `React.FC<PortfolioDriveProps>`, ensuring the components correctly receive and utilize the `isAdmin` flag. I'm focusing on the integration and testing this locally to ensure I don't break the build.


**Enhancing Data Persistence**

I'm now integrating `localStorage` for improved data persistence within the application. I'm focusing on initializing the `videos` state from `localStorage`, ensuring changes made in admin mode persist across reloads. This addresses the ephemeral nature of the initial solution, making the "Add" feature usable, even locally. I'll utilize `guizera_drive_videos` and `guizera_insta_reels` as the `localStorage` keys to store the respective videos.


**Confirming the Approach**

I'm solidifying the `App.tsx` and portfolio components. I've switched to `window.location.search` for more direct admin mode detection. I'm focusing now on ensuring data persistence using `localStorage`. 2.  **Limpeza de Cache (v17):** Atualizei a versão do armazenamento local para `guizera_drive_videos_v17`. Isso garante que qualquer versão antiga ou problemática dos vídeos salva no navegador do usuário seja resetada para a lista padrão correta.
3.  **Fallback Visual:** Adicionei uma instrução clara abaixo do player caso o navegador do usuário seja extremamente restritivo, e destaquei o botão "Abrir no Drive" como alternativa garantida.

Essas mudanças devem permitir que você clique no play, desmute e assista sem pausas inesperadas.

Solução (CSS do Modal):

Defina a largura para width: 95vw; (ocupar 95% da largura da tela).

Garanta que o iframe ou tag video dentro dele tenha width: 100% e height: auto (ou uma altura definida que respeite o aspecto).

I'm also considering the effect of `aspect-ratio` on the browser's width calculation and will check to ensure my height and width adjustments work well together with the `object-cover` property.


**Implementing Flexible Video Sizing**

The current focus is on maximizing the mobile video display. I've switched the vertical video's container to `w-full max-w-[50vh] aspect-[9/16] md:w-auto md:h-[85vh]` in App.tsx. I am ensuring padding is appropriate across different devices and that the `PortfolioInsta.tsx` is being reviewed for the correct `h-[350px]` height.


**Finalizing Video Adjustments**

I've simplified the mobile vertical video class to prioritize width: `w-full aspect-[9/16] md:w-auto md:h-[85vh]`, removing the `max-h` constraint. This addresses the "squashed width" complaint, ensuring the video uses the full width on mobile. I also updated the overlay padding and adjusted the horizontal video class accordingly.

Aqui estão as correções de emergência solicitadas.

**Resumo das Alterações:**

1.  **App.tsx (Modal de Vídeo):**
    *   **Padding do Overlay:** Reduzido drasticamente para `p-2` no mobile (era `p-4`), garantindo que o vídeo possa encostar quase nas bordas. No desktop, aumentei para `md:p-10` para dar respiro.
    *   **Largura do Vídeo:** Para vídeos verticais no mobile, forcei `w-full` (ocupar toda a largura disponível dentro do padding) e mantive o `aspect-[9/16]`. Isso impede o cálculo de altura máxima de "esmagar" a largura. O vídeo agora será largo e alto.

2.  **PortfolioInsta.tsx (Grid de Verticais):**
    *   **Altura dos Cards:** Aumentada para `h-[350px]` no mobile conforme solicitado, garantindo uma grade uniforme e imagens maiores.
    *   **Ajuste de Imagem:** Mantido o `w-full h-full` com `object-cover` para preenchimento total.

payload.text:
CORREÇÃO CRÍTICA DE UX MOBILE: PROBLEMA DO "CLICK DUPLO" NOS VÍDEOS

No iPhone (e outros dispositivos móveis), o usuário precisa clicar três vezes para assistir a um vídeo da seção "Produções Verticais":

Primeiro toque: Ativa o estado de hover (mostrando a capa achatada).

Segundo toque: Abre o modal do player.

Terceiro toque: Dá play no vídeo.

Precisamos corrigir esse comportamento para que o primeiro toque já abra o modal e o vídeo esteja pronto para tocar.

Aplique as seguintes correções no componente de thumbnails (provavelmente PortfolioItem.tsx ou similar) e no Modal de Vídeo:

1. Eliminar o Estado de Hover no Mobile:

Utilize uma media query para garantir que o efeito de hover (que muda a capa, aplica zoom ou mostra o botão de play) NÃO SEJA APLICADO em dispositivos com tela de toque (@media (hover: none) ou telas menores que 768px).

No Mobile: O botão de play e o título devem estar SEMPRE VISÍVEIS por cima da capa.

O evento de clique (onClick) deve ser disparado imediatamente no primeiro toque.

2. Auto-Play e Comportamento do Modal:

Quando o modal abrir no mobile, o vídeo já deve estar pronto para dar play (sem precisar de um terceiro clique).

Certifique-se de que o player (YouTube ou Drive) esteja configurado com autoplay=1 (se possível) e mute=0 (para o usuário controlar o som).

Nota: Em alguns navegadores mobile, o autoplay de vídeo com som é bloqueado. O ideal é abrir o player, e um toque no centro do vídeo já o inicie.

3. Correção da Capa Achatada:

O problema da capa "achatada" no primeiro toque é causado por uma regra de CSS de hover. Garanta que a imagem da capa tenha sempre height: 100%, width: 100% e object-fit: cover, e que nenhuma regra de hover altere essas propriedades no celular.

Objetivo: No celular, o usuário vê a grade. Ele toca uma vez em um vídeo. O modal abre imediatamente com o player pronto para ser iniciado com apenas mais um toque.

**Reviewing the User's Issue**

I'm currently focused on the user request. The core problem appears to be a frustrating mobile UX for "Vertical Productions" videos, specifically on iPhones. Multiple taps are required to start playback, which is a major pain point. Now, I'm working to identify if there are specific videos or if it is a general issue with the system.


**Addressing UX Pain Points**

I'm now diving into the specifics of the double-tap issue. I've pinpointed that the "hover" effect, triggered by the first tap, is the culprit. This leads to a flattened image and necessitates a second tap to open the modal. Inside the modal, a third tap is then needed for video playback. I'm focusing on making a more streamlined mobile experience, aiming for a single tap to open the modal and immediately play the video. Also, I will address the CSS, making sure it applies 'object-fit: cover' to prevent those flattened thumbnails.


**Eliminating Hover Interference**

I'm zeroing in on the interaction issue. My investigation strongly suggests that the `group-hover` styles are the source of the trouble on mobile devices. I've confirmed that iOS is misinterpreting the first tap as a hover action. This is making it so a subsequent tap is required, and I suspect this stems from the `group` class and `hover:` states on children.  I'm now evaluating solutions.


**Improving Video Embeds**

I'm now investigating video embeds. `getYoutubeEmbedUrl` already uses autoplay, which is good. I'm noting that `getDriveEmbedUrl` uses `/preview`, which often requires a click. The user's three-click problem may reduce to two clicks with the grid fix. I'm focusing on the `PortfolioInsta.tsx` grid. The `hover` style is likely the culprit on mobile, causing style shifts and requiring an extra tap. I will fix this. I am now trying to make those styles static on mobile devices.


**Optimizing Mobile Interactions**

I'm presently revising the CSS, specifically the `PortfolioInsta.tsx` grid. My goal is to simplify it for mobile devices, making interactions more fluid. I've noted the `transform: 'scale(1.02)'` on hover can look strange on devices with touch screens. I am making it so that these styles are static on mobile to fix the issue. I am also implementing `pointer-events-none` on overlay elements. My next step will be to verify `PortfolioDrive.tsx` for consistent behavior.


**Improving Mobile Interaction**

I'm now focusing on a specific mobile issue, and it's looking quite promising. I've realized the primary culprit behind the double-tap problem is the `:hover` style applied to elements. Specifically, on touch devices, a tap is often misconstrued as a hover, leading to the need for a second tap to trigger the actual click. I'm working to isolate and mitigate the impact of `group-hover` which is the current source of our trouble. I'm also addressing the "flattened image" issue which is caused by the same effects, by removing problematic transitions on touch devices. I'm experimenting with a media query to apply hover styles only when a hover-capable device is detected.


**Fine-tuning Embeds & Interactions**

I'm now implementing the changes. In `PortfolioInsta.tsx`, I've adjusted the container and iframe classes as planned, removing problematic `hover:` classes and transitions for mobile. I'm verifying the `pointer-events` logic to ensure click events propagate correctly. In `urlHelpers.ts`, I've confirmed YouTube's `autoplay=1` is working and noted the limitations of Drive embeds and mobile autoplay restrictions. I will also check `mute=0` and adjust the other videos to match the settings.


**Streamlining Grid Elements**

I'm now revising the code in `PortfolioInsta.tsx` and `PortfolioDrive.tsx` to fix the double/triple-tap issue. I'm removing the `hover` styles on mobile, applying them only for medium-sized screens and larger. I'm also ensuring the `object-fit: cover` property is enforced for consistent image display. I'll test the changes.


**Resolving Hover Interference**

I'm now implementing the changes. I'm focusing on the `PortfolioInsta.tsx` and `PortfolioDrive.tsx` components to eliminate hover issues on mobile. I will strictly define dimensions and ensure they don't change on hover to prevent unnecessary animations. The `md:` prefix will be used as a proxy for desktop/mouse interactions, to ensure hover effects are triggered only on the appropriate devices. I'm also ensuring YouTube embeds use `autoplay=1`.


**Refining Modal Autoplay**

I'm now investigating the modal behavior in `App.tsx`. I'll explore integrating autoplay features within the modal component, making use of the existing `autoplay=1` parameter for YouTube embeds, and considering adjustments to improve Drive embed handling. I'll test these fixes alongside the thumbnail improvements. I am also investigating whether a single-click solution is better than autoplay, for the user's overall satisfaction.


**Improving Embed Autoplay**

I'm now integrating autoplay capabilities for both YouTube and Google Drive embeds, especially for the modal view, by strategically adding URL parameters. I've updated the `urlHelpers.ts` file to generate Drive links with `autoplay=1` (where possible), recognizing the limitations of Google Drive's autoplay implementation. The YouTube embed's `autoplay=1` is confirmed, and I will be testing all media types with modal fixes soon.


**Execute Fixes and Verify**

I'm now putting the pieces together. I'm focusing on making the grid a single-click experience for the user. I will address both the `PortfolioInsta` and `PortfolioDrive` components to achieve this. I will remove the `group` class from the parent or make sure that the `group-hover` styles only apply on medium-sized screens and larger. I will also be making sure the `pointer-events-none` is enabled on any overlay layers and that the `z-index` values are correct so that the user's click hits the parent div. I'll make sure the autoplay functionality is working as expected. Finally, I will verify the changes to ensure a smooth user experience.

Para corrigir o problema do "click duplo" (comportamento nativo do iOS/Android onde o primeiro toque aciona o `:hover` e o segundo o `click`) e garantir a experiência fluida solicitada, farei alterações focadas em remover estados de hover em dispositivos móveis e ajustar a detecção de toque.

Aqui está o plano de execução:

1.  **`components/PortfolioInsta.tsx`**: Refatoração completa das classes Tailwind. Vou prefixar todas as interações de estado (hover, transition, transform) com `md:`. Isso garante que, no celular, o navegador entenda o elemento como um "botão simples" estático, disparando o clique imediatamente no primeiro toque.
2.  **`components/PortfolioDrive.tsx`**: Aplicarei a mesma lógica para consistência no portfólio horizontal.
3.  **`utils/urlHelpers.ts`**: Adicionarei parâmetros explícitos para tentar forçar o autoplay onde possível.

Correção UX Mobile: Aplicação da mesma lógica de 'toque único' para o portfólio horizontal.
Garantia de autoplay na URL do YouTube.
